title: Classical modular newform
description: The interesting case: the object is infinite but the identifier must be finite. A newform is determined by its coefficients up to the Sturm bound, so identity is well defined only when enough of them are given — "enough" being a theorem rather than a convention. A submission truncated below the bound is not a different form, it is an object we cannot yet identify, and it should be rejected rather than assigned an identifier that a longer expansion would contradict.

coefficients.description: a_1, a_2, ... listed from n = 1, to at least the Sturm bound. policy: primary. convention: newform-normalized.
